newsitem.title: CANADA: AA to accept cargo upto strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: AA to accept cargo upto strike deadline.

text.p: American Airlines, facing a Saturday strike deadline by its 10,000 pilots, said it will keep accepting cargo right up to Friday if it can be delivered before the threatened walkout.
The airline has no plans to fly if there is a strike but expects normal operations Friday, says Mark Najarian, vice-president of U.S. cargo sales.
It will accept and carry point to point traffic up to and including Friday, he added.
"What you will probably see us do (before Friday) is minimize the cargo that will be in our terminals Friday night," Najarian said from American headquarters in Fort Worth, Texas.
"We wouldn't want to have cargo that originates in Southeast Asia destined for Latin America getting stuck somewhere in the middle" (at one of AA's U.S. stations), he said.
"So the first thing we may do is limit the two- or three-leg shipments so that the goods of the shipper and consignee are not stuck in that city.
That decision could be made on Wednesday, he said.

Other sensitive traffic the airline may embargo before Friday are live animals, human remains, some types of dangerous goods - things so sensitive "we wouldn't like to have any kind of disruption in the quality of service," he said.

In the meantime, individual customers are making their own contingency plans to deal with a strike, "and I think the best thing we can do is be honest with them as events unfold so they can get their contingency plans into play," said Najarian.
"We have a letter going to our key accounts every day, giving them an update based on the events that have happened the previous day," he said.
